LDL-C management simplified: The National Lipid Association lipid simplified series.
items.abstract: Atherosclerotic heart disease is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, with the magnitude of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) event reduction being proportional to the degree of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) lowering. The 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association/Multisociety Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia highlights the need to achieve LDL-C levels that are "lower for longer" with treatment targeted to individual ASCVD risk. Current risk estimators, biomarkers, and imaging tools have allowed for the improved discrimination of ASCVD risk to select those who benefit most and guide the intensity of treatment. With the combination of optimal lifestyle therapy and an armamentarium of lipid-lowering agents, achieving optimal levels is attainable and essential to cardiovascular health. Referrals to lipid specialists should be considered for complex care to increase access to advanced therapeutics and manage complex cases. Toward that goal, lipid panel testing should be done regularly in adults to evaluate ASCVD risk and to monitor for effectiveness and adherence to LDL-C-lowering treatment. The following manuscript is intended to serve as a "simplified" guide to the management of LDL-C in clinical practice.

items.title: Cardiac and natriuretic peptide profiles by subtype and sex in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) encompasses heterogeneous metabolic phenotypes. We examined associations of MASLD subtypes with epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) thickness, left atrial volume index (LAVI), and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and whether these associations differed by sex. In a cross-sectional analysis of 6181 adults undergoing concurrent abdominal ultrasonography and transthoracic echocardiography, participants were classified as No MASLD, Lean MASLD, Obese MASLD without diabetes, or Obese MASLD with diabetes (2023 Delphi criteria). Multivariable linear regression and sex-stratified analyses were used. Obese subtypes had greater EAT thickness, with the largest contrast in those with diabetes (β = 0.030 cm; p  2 ; p  2 was 3.0% for log NT-proBNP and 0.6-1.0% for structural outcomes. Estimates in women were similar after menopause adjustment. MASLD subtypes were associated with different EAT, LAVI, and NT-proBNP profiles, with differences by sex. Structural contrasts were modest, whereas the association with NT-proBNP was larger. The clinical significance of these findings requires prospective evaluation.

items.title: Prevalence and prognostic significance of intracranial lesions assessed with MRI in infective endocarditis patients: Data from the Vesuve study.
items.abstract: Infective endocarditis (IE) is a life-threatening disease. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is efficient to detect cerebral IE related lesions, which are known to worsen prognosis. Systematic use of MRI remains controversial due to insufficient scientific evidence. This work was aimed at clarifying the prognostic value of this imaging method in the context of IE. The VESUVE study is a retrospective registry of patients with definite IE according to the modified Duke criteria, who had a brain MRI and were hospitalized between the 1st of November 2015 and the 15th of February 2019 in a Lyon University Hospital. All MRI were analyzed by the same senior neuroradiologist. Prognosis was evaluated by the mortality rate at 6 months. Among 212 patients, 162 were considered to have an abnormal MRI (76.4%). Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) was present in 125 patients (60.4%), intracranial hemorrhage in 8 patients (3.8%), hemorrhagic transformation in 41 patients (19.5%), subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) in 26 patients (12.4%), cerebral microbleed in 130 patients (62.5%), intracranial mycotic aneurysm in 10 patients (5.1%), sulcal microaneurysm in 45 patients (23.6%) and abscess in 3 patients (1.5%). Mortality rate at 6 months was 19% (37 patients deceased). AIS (26.9% mortality, 31 patients deceased, OR 5.11) and SAH (44% mortality, 11 patients deceased, OR 4.32) were linked to mortality. The presence of AIS or SAH on brain MRI is independently linked to mortality in IE patients. This strengthens the prognostic value of MRI in the assessment of IE.

items.title: Role of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging in the diagnosis of chronic constrictive pericarditis revealed by Pick's syndrome: A case report.
items.abstract: Chronic constrictive pericarditis (CCP), or Pick's syndrome, is a rare but severe inflammatory disease of the pericardium, often difficult to distinguish from restrictive cardiomyopathy without multimodality imaging. In sub-Saharan Africa, tuberculosis remains the leading cause. We report the case of a 37-year-old woman with a history of post-partum hypertension, admitted for a three-month history of exertional dyspnoea, lower-limb oedema and retrosternal chest pain in a febrile, tuberculosis-suggestive context. Examination revealed isolated right heart failure with a pericardial knock. Echocardiography and cardiac MRI showed pericardial thickening and circumferential detachment, bi-atrial dilatation and a septal bounce, with late gadolinium enhancement and T1/T2 mapping consistent with active pericardial inflammation, confirming an evolving, inflammatory form of CCP. Coronary CT angiography excluded coexisting coronary disease and revealed tuberculous pulmonary sequelae. Under corticosteroids, antituberculous therapy and symptomatic management, the patient improved clinically, allowing pericardiectomy to be deferred. This case highlights the value of cardiac MRI in the early diagnosis of inflammatory, potentially reversible forms of CCP, helping to avoid upfront surgery and guide targeted medical management, particularly in tuberculosis-endemic regions.

items.title: Autoimmune encephalitis and paraneoplastic neurological syndrome: A practical guide for clinicians.
items.abstract: Autoimmune encephalitis and paraneoplastic neurological syndromes comprise a group of disorders affecting both the central and peripheral nervous systems, with an increasing incidence likely attributable to increased clinical awareness and continuous advances in diagnostic methods. These conditions are characterized by an aberrant immune response and often require the involvement of multiple specialties, including neurology, pediatrics, oncology, immunology, and intensive care medicine. In this review, we aimed to provide clinicians with essential knowledge for recognizing clinical syndromes suggestive of these entities, thereby facilitating the establishment of an appropriate diagnostic and therapeutic approach.

items.title: Neoadjuvant Therapy in Patients with Upper Tract Urothelial Cancer: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
items.abstract: The role of neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in patients with upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) remains controversial, mainly because of the lack of high-level evidence. We aim to update the evidence on NAC regarding pathological and oncological outcomes in patients with nonmetastatic UTUC. Moreover, we also aimed to give an overview of neoadjuvant immunotherapy (NAI) in the current clinical scenario. A systematic review of 41 studies on NAC and NAI (eight prospective studies [PS] or randomized clinical trials [RCTs] and 33 retrospective studies [RS]) was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Outcomes of interest included pathological complete response (pCR), pathological partial response (pPR), pathological downstaging, overall survival (OS), cancer-specific survival (CSS), and disease-free survival (DFS). Pooled analyses were performed using effect sizes for pathological outcomes and hazard ratios (HRs) for survival outcomes. Finally, 5-yr proportions were summarized when a 5-yr time threshold was available. Of the 41 articles, 30 (five PS or RCTs and 25 RS) were eligible for meta-analysis (n = 2384 patients). The pooled pCR, pPR, and pathological downstaging rates were, respectively, 11% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 10-12), 44% (95% CI: 38-50), and 20% (95% CI: 10-37). Compared with radical nephroureterectomy (RNU), NAC was associated with pooled HRs of 0.56 (95% CI: 0.39-0.80) for OS, 0.47 (95% CI: 0.26-0.85) for CSS, and 0.55 (95% CI: 0.24-1.26) for DFS. Evidence on NAI remains limited in terms of sample size and is primarily derived from early-phase studies. NAC was associated with favorable oncological outcomes compared with RNU alone. Nevertheless, the absence of prospective randomized studies limits the strength of the evidence, and further high-quality trials are warranted to confirm these findings.

Intestinal Candida albicans promotes HCC progression and anti-PD-1 resistance via IL-17A and Trem2 + macrophages.
items.abstract: Whether intestinal fungal dysbiosis contributes to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) remains unclear. We investigated how gut Candida albicans influences HCC progression, immune remodeling, and response to ICI therapy. Fecal and tumor samples from patients with HCC, liver cirrhosis, and healthy controls were analyzed using ITS2 sequencing, immune profiling, and correlation analyses. Mechanistic studies focused on four complementary autochthonous murine HCC models and cell-based assays, integrating single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing, genetic and pharmacologic perturbations, Kaede photoconversion, fungal antigen recall assays, antifungal treatment, and anti-PD-1 therapy. Fecal C. albicans abundance was higher in HCC patients and was associated with advanced disease, shorter overall survival, and reduced durable clinical benefit. Across HCC models, C. albicans gavage increased tumor burden and induced a Th17/IL-17A-skewed microenvironment characterized by Trem2 + macrophage accumulation and impaired CD8 + T cell infiltration and function. Antifungal treatment attenuated tumor progression, whereas IL-17A blockade or deficiency largely abrogated C. albicans-associated tumor promotion. Mechanistically, IL-17A induced tumor-derived MCP-1 through ACT1-TRAF6-TAK1 signaling to recruit macrophages and upregulated PAI-1, which activated TGF-β/Smad3 signaling to promote an immunosuppressive Trem2 + macrophage state. These macrophages limited CD8 + T cell recruitment and effector function through coordinated CXCL10 repression and GAL-1 induction, while potentially reinforcing Th17 responses through IL-1β and IL-6. Kaede photoconversion demonstrated enhanced mesenteric lymph node-to-liver Th17 trafficking, while fungal antigen recall assays revealed preferential Th17 responsiveness to C. albicans. C. albicans also impaired anti-PD-1 efficacy in vivo, whereas antifungal treatment partially restored therapeutic responsiveness. Intestinal C. albicans promotes HCC progression and anti-PD-1 resistance through an IL-17A-Trem2 + macrophage circuit, supporting its potential as a biomarker and therapeutic target. Intestinal fungal dysbiosis is increasingly recognized as a component of the gut-liver axis, but its functional contribution to HCC has remained poorly defined. Our study identifies intestinal Candida albicans as a promoter of HCC progression in experimental models and delineates an IL-17A-MCP-1/PAI-1-Trem2 + macrophage circuit that links fungal exposure to impaired CD8 + T-cell immunity and reduced response to PD-1 blockade. These findings are relevant to researchers and clinicians seeking microbiome-associated determinants of HCC progression and immunotherapy resistance. Fecal C. albicans abundance and components of this immune circuit may warrant evaluation as biomarkers for patient stratification and as potential targets for combination therapy. However, the clinical associations reported here are based on modest observational cohorts, and antifungal treatment was tested as a proof-of-concept intervention in mice. Larger prospective studies and more selective therapeutic approaches will therefore be required before these findings can inform clinical management.

items.title: Entamoeba invadens infection contributes to juvenile mortality in captive sea turtles.
items.abstract: Sea turtles are globally threatened marine reptiles, and infectious diseases are increasingly recognized as important causes of juvenile mortality. However, the etiology and pathogenesis of many diseases, including amoebiasis, remain poorly understood. Systemic amoebic lesions have been reported in sea turtles, yet the causative Entamoeba species has never been identified at the species level using molecular methods. We therefore investigated the etiology and pathogenesis of fatal amoebiasis using carcasses of 15 captive juvenile sea turtles (three loggerhead, Caretta caretta, and 12 green turtles, Chelonia mydas), integrating histopathological and molecular approaches. Histopathology revealed severe necrotizing enteritis, hepatitis, and pneumonia with abundant amoebic trophozoites and cysts. Polymerase chain reaction, Sanger sequencing, and in situ hybridization identified Entamoeba invadens in the intestine, liver, and lungs; 18S rRNA amplicon sequencing also detected E. invadens in fecal and intestinal samples. Phylogenetic analysis showed that the sea turtle-derived sequence clustered with E. invadens sequences from other reptile hosts. Bacterial and fungal aggregates were also observed within necrotic lesions, and 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing detected diverse bacterial communities without a consistently dominant taxon, consistent with secondary microbial translocation following intestinal barrier disruption rather than primary bacterial infection. These findings provide the first evidence that E. invadens causes fatal systemic amoebiasis in juvenile sea turtles and are consistent with polymicrobial invasion following parasite-induced intestinal damage. This study establishes a pathological and molecular basis for diagnosing systemic amoebiasis in sea turtles and has important implications for wildlife disease ecology and sea turtle conservation.

items.title: HBs proteins do not reveal their genomic origin.
Small molecules inhibit hepatitis B and D virus infection by binding the small surface antigen.
items.abstract: Current therapies for chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection effectively suppress viral replication but do not achieve a functional cure. Targeting viral entry represents a promising strategy to complement existing treatments. Small-molecule compounds were identified through structure-based virtual screening targeting SHBs (small hepatitis B surface antigen). HBV infection models using HepG2-NTCP cells and primary human hepatocytes were established to investigate the antiviral activities and underlying mechanisms of these compounds in vitro. Molecular docking analyses were performed to predict the potential binding regions of the small molecules with SHBs. In addition, we performed mutagenesis based on the predicted interaction residues, followed by functional assays to validate the docking predictions. Assays in the HBV infection model showed that isotretinoin, ciprofibrate, and caffeic acid significantly reduced HBsAg, HBeAg, and HBV pregenomic RNA levels when administered concurrently with HBV infection. Biophysical and biochemical assays demonstrated that these compounds interacted with SHBs. In addition, molecular docking and site-directed mutagenesis-based functional assays suggested that the interaction sites may involve the AGL region. Mechanistically, the compounds mainly acted during the early stage of infection and reduced HBV attachment and internalization-associated signals. In addition, these compounds inhibited HDV infection, supporting their activity against HBV envelope-mediated viral entry. Our findings suggest that these small molecules are promising candidates for developing novel entry inhibitors targeting SHBs, which may enhance therapeutic options against HBV and HDV.

items.title: New paradigms in Hepatitis D: screening, treatment, and the path to cure.
items.abstract: Chronic hepatitis D virus infection, also known as chronic hepatitis delta, remains the most severe form of chronic viral hepatitis, associated with accelerated liver disease progression, cirrhosis, decompensation, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Recent years have seen major advances in screening strategies and antiviral therapies for hepatitis D. This review discusses evidence supporting broader hepatitis D screening among hepatitis B surface antigen-positive individuals and practical considerations for implementation across epidemiological settings, and reviews current and emerging treatments - entry inhibition (bulevirtide), prenylation inhibition (lonafarnib), immune-modulatory therapies (pegylated interferons), and hepatitis B surface antigen-targeting approaches (tobevibart, elebsiran, brelovitug, nucleic acid polymers) - focusing on treatment response and durability of viral suppression. In conclusion, emerging therapies have substantially improved antiviral efficacy, shifting the focus of hepatitis D management from on-treatment suppression toward durable off-treatment control and functional cure, changing the diagnosis, treatment, and long-term management of chronic hepatitis D.

items.title: Genetic diversity of inclusion body hepatitis-associated fowl adenoviruses in Thailand from 2014 to 2025.
items.abstract: Inclusion body hepatitis (IBH), caused by fowl adenoviruses (FAdVs), is an important disease affecting poultry health and production. Limited cross-protection among heterologous FAdV serotypes makes molecular surveillance essential for guiding disease prevention and control. Nevertheless, serotype distribution and genetic diversity of IBH-associated FAdVs in Thailand remain limited. To address this gap, a retrospective molecular study analyzed 56 FAdV-positive chickens associated with IBH or suspected IBH that were submitted for diagnostic investigation between 2014 and 2025. A partial hexon L1-loop region was amplified, sequenced, and analyzed by phylogenetic and deduced amino-acid comparisons. The isolates were classified into three serotypes: FAdV-8b, FAdV-11, and FAdV-2. FAdV-8b was the most frequently detected serotype, accounting for 30/56 isolates (53.57%), followed by FAdV-11 with 23/56 isolates (41.07%) and FAdV-2 with 3/56 isolates (5.36%). Temporal differences in serotype distribution were observed among the sequenced diagnostic submissions. All sequences collected during 2014-2018 belonged to species D and included FAdV-2 and FAdV-11. FAdV-8b was first detected in this dataset in 2019, and it accounted for 30 of the 35 sequences obtained during 2019-2025. Phylogenetic analysis separated Thai FAdV-8b isolates into three groups and FAdV-2 isolates into two groups, while FAdV-11 isolates were highly conserved within the analyzed region. Group-associated amino-acid substitutions were mainly located in the hypervariable regions of the Hexon L1-loop, suggesting potential relevance to within-serotype antigenic variation. Overall, these findings provide updated molecular epidemiological information on IBH-associated FAdVs in Thailand and underscore the need for continued molecular surveillance to inform diagnostic strategies and vaccine selection.

items.title: Human cytochrome P450 27A1-a variety of reactions, applications, and potentials for drug targeting.
items.abstract: The human cytochrome P450 (P450) 27A1 enzyme is most often described as a liver enzyme that initiates the alternative (acidic) pathway of bile acid synthesis. Although this is certainly an important role for this enzyme, research has shown that it has a significantly wider role to play in normal physiology and disease pathology. This minireview aims to provide a useful reference for studies showing the many ways P450 27A1 is involved in human health and to help researchers access useful methods. The distribution, expression, and regulation of the enzyme in both normal and disease states are discussed. A catalog of steady-state kinetics experiments is included. A review of methods for recombinant expression, inhibition, and studying redox partner interactions is also included. Two key examples of connections to disease, breast cancer and neurodegeneration, are explored as possible applications of P450 27A1 research and illustrations of the complexity of the role of the enzyme. Finally, a few key areas of needed clarification are suggested with hopes to inspire researchers to contribute to work in this important area. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Human cytochrome P450 27A1 and its products, particularly 27-hydroxycholesterol, are increasingly connected to variety of diseases such as cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis, atherosclerosis, multiple cancers, and neurodegenerative diseases. This review explores the systemic physiological control and basic enzymology of cytochrome P450 27A1 to facilitate collaboration across these different biomedical dimensions toward advancing diagnosis and treatment.

items.title: Hereditary Pancreatic Cancer.
items.abstract: Pancreatic cancer remains one of the deadliest malignancies, with most patients presenting at advanced stages and experiencing poor survival outcomes. Approximately 10% to 15% of cases are associated with inherited genetic susceptibility, highlighting the critical role of germline genetic testing and family history assessment. Multiple hereditary cancer syndromes, including those involving BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM, PALB2, CDKN2A, STK11, TP53, and select Lynch syndrome mismatch repair genes, confer increased risk of pancreatic cancer. Universal germline testing, cascade testing of at-risk relatives, and individualized risk assessment facilitate precision oncology and early detection. Screening for pancreatic cancer using select imaging modalities enables earlier-stage diagnosis and improves survival.

Practical considerations of gadoxetate disodium contrast in MRI-guided liver SBRT for primary and secondary liver tumors: optimizing image quality and patient throughput.
items.abstract: Optimal implementation of gadoxetate disodium injection (GDI) in liver-directed MR-guided online adaptive radiotherapy (MRgART) remains poorly characterized. Herein, we evaluated the impact of GDI on physician-reported imaging metrics and quantitative contouring variability during liver MRgART planning. Patients were scanned using a 0.35T MRI onboard the MR-guided LINAC. Pre- and post-contrast TRUFI images were captured at multiple timepoints up to 30 minutes (5-10-minute intervals) following GDI. Four radiation oncologists independently scored each tumor on a 5-point scale (1: poor; 5: excellent) evaluating imaging metrics, such as tumor visualization, border delineation, and image degradation from artifacts. Responses were stratified into pre-contrast, "early" post-contrast (1-15 minutes), and "late" post-contrast (20-30 minutes). Physicians then contoured gross tumor volume (GTV) for 6 patients with either optimal or non-optimal image characteristics. Inter- and intra-observer variability was assessed using Sørensen-Dice coefficient (DICE), Hausdorff distance (HD), volume of tumor not treated (VTNT), and volume of healthy liver erroneously treated (VHL). Comparisons were performed using Mann-Whitney U-test or Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test, as applicable. Twenty-three patients with 37 total liver tumors were treated using MRgART (median 50 Gy; 3-5 fractions). Late post-contrast imaging significantly improved tumor visualization (4.45) compared to early post-contrast (3.73; p 3 to 0.68 cm 3 (p<0.001). GDI administration 20-30 minutes prior to MRgART planning significantly enhances both physician-reported image quality and quantitative contouring accuracy. Its use should be considered in MRgART workflows to minimize potential geographic miss and optimize treatment delivery.
